aspects.says: In Java 21 a case null label handles a null selector, and it makes the compiler require the switch statement to cover every value.
basis: section:A null Selector Throws Before Any Label Is Compared, default Included

aspects.says: default is a label like the others: its position doesn't change which values reach it, and a default placed before other cases falls through into them.
basis: section:A Case Label Is Where Execution Enters, and It Runs On Until a break

aspects.says: A classic switch statement over an enum, without case null, is not checked for coverage, so a new constant runs nothing unless a default throws; the old switch still matches constants by name after only the enum is recompiled.
basis: section:A Switch Statement Over an Enum Needn't Name Every Constant, So a New Constant Runs Nothing

aspects.says: A switch statement jumps to the matching label and runs every statement below it, through later labels, until a break, return or throw, so a missing break runs the next case and cumulative behaviour can be written by falling through.
basis: section:A Case Label Is Where Execution Enters, and It Runs On Until a break

aspects.says: Every label is a distinct constant expression that fits the selector; a final variable of a wrapper type, or one set by a method call, is not a constant.
basis: section:The Selector Is an int-Compatible Type, a String or an Enum, and Every Label Is a Distinct Constant

aspects.says: A value that no label names, in a switch without a default, runs nothing and raises no error.
basis: section:A Case Label Is Where Execution Enters, and It Runs On Until a break
section:A Switch Statement Over an Enum Needn't Name Every Constant, So a New Constant Runs Nothing

aspects.says: A protocol value normalised with toLowerCase() depends on the default locale (a Turkish I lowers to a dotless i); toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) doesn't.
basis: section:A String Switch Matches With equals, So It Is Exact and Case-Sensitive

aspects.says: A null selector throws NullPointerException before any label is compared, so a default doesn't catch it; the code checks for null first or uses case null.
basis: section:A null Selector Throws Before Any Label Is Compared, default Included

aspects.says: A classic switch takes char, byte, short, int, their wrappers, String or an enum; long, float, double and boolean are refused because the switch instructions are keyed by int.
basis: section:The Selector Is an int-Compatible Type, a String or an Enum, and Every Label Is a Distinct Constant
aspects.reason: a compile-time rule: a switch on a long doesn't compile, so no test can run it

aspects.says: A switch on a String matches with hashCode and equals: a value built at run time matches its literal, and the match is exact and case-sensitive.
basis: section:A String Switch Matches With equals, So It Is Exact and Case-Sensitive

aspects.says: The whole switch body is one block for declarations, so a name declared under one label can't be declared again under another.
basis: section:A Case Label Is Where Execution Enters, and It Runs On Until a break
aspects.reason: a compile-time rule: a solution that breaks it doesn't compile, so there is no wrong solution a test can run
